extracted.intended_audience: users of Singular (computational algebraists) working with D-modules / Weyl algebras (dmodapp.lib and dmodvar.lib)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in Singular's dmodapp.lib and dmodvar.lib that operate on (parametric) Weyl algebras and compute D-module objects (initial ideals, restrictions, de Rham cohomology, characteristic varieties, Bernstein-Sato data, Fourier transforms, etc.). Each entry lists usage, return type, assumptions and important options.

rubrics_metrics.name: initialMalgrange
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: initialMalgrange(f[,a,b,v]); f poly, a,b optional ints, v opt. intvec. Return: ring, Weyl algebra induced by basering, extended by two new vars t,Dt. Purpose: computes the initial Malgrange ideal of a given polynomial w.r.t. the weight vector (-1,0...,0,1,0,...,0) such that the weight of t is -1 and the weight of Dt is 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume the basering is commutative and over a field of characteristic 0. Activate the output ring with setring. The returned ring contains the ideal 'inF' (the initial ideal of the Malgrange ideal of f). Varnames of the basering should not include t and Dt. If a<>0, std is used for Gröbner basis computations, otherwise slimgb is used. If b<>0, a matrix ordering is used; otherwise a block ordering. If a positive weight vector v is given, a specific homogenization weight (d,v[1],...,v[n],1,d+1-v[1],...,d+1-v[n]) is used (d = weighted degree of f); otherwise v defaults to (1,...,1). Display controlled by printlevel (>=1 progress messages, >=2 all debug). Example usage and sample inF entries are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: initialIdealW
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: initialIdealW(I,u,v[,s,t,w]); I ideal, u,v intvecs, s,t optional ints, w optional intvec. Return: ideal, Gröbner basis (GB) of initial ideal of input ideal w.r.t. weights u and v. Purpose: computes the initial ideal with respect to given weights in the n-th Weyl algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is the n-th Weyl algebra in characteristic 0 and variables ordered as x(1..n),D(1..n) with D(i) the differential operator for x(i). u and v are weight vectors for x and D respectively. If s<>0 use std, otherwise slimgb. If t<>0 use a matrix ordering, otherwise block ordering. If w is given with exactly 2*n strictly positive entries it is used as homogenization weight; otherwise (1,...,1) is used. Display controlled by printlevel.

rubrics_metrics.name: inForm
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: inForm(I,w); I ideal or poly, w intvec. Return: ideal (generated by initial forms of generators of I w.r.t. w) or poly (initial form of input poly). Purpose: computes the initial form of an ideal or a polynomial w.r.t. the weight w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The size of weight vector must equal the number of variables of the basering. Examples show different weight vectors producing different initial forms. Display behavior per printlevel.

rubrics_metrics.name: restrictionIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: restrictionIdeal(I,w[,eng,m,G]); I ideal, w intvec, eng and m optional ints, G optional ideal. Return: ring (a Weyl algebra) containing an ideal 'resIdeal'. Purpose: computes the restriction ideal of a holonomic ideal to the subspace defined by variables corresponding to non-zero entries of the intvec w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is n-th Weyl algebra (char 0) with usual variable ordering and identities; assume I is holonomic and w is n-dimensional with non-negative entries. The output ring is the Weyl algebra defined by the zero entries of w and contains 'resIdeal' (the restriction ideal). If there are no zero entries, input ring is returned. If eng<>0 use std, otherwise slimgb. Optional m: minimal integer root of b-function of I wrt (-w,w) can be specified. Optional G: specify a Gröbner basis of I wrt (-w,w) (initial form of G generates the initial ideal); assumptions on m and G are not checked. Display controlled by printlevel.

rubrics_metrics.name: restrictionModule
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: restrictionModule(I,w[,eng,m,G]); I ideal, w intvec, eng and m optional ints, G optional ideal. Return: ring (a Weyl algebra) containing a module 'resMod'. Purpose: computes the restriction module of a holonomic ideal to the subspace defined by variables corresponding to non-zero entries of w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same baseline assumptions as restrictionIdeal: n-th Weyl algebra over field char 0, I holonomic, w non-negative. Output ring is Weyl algebra defined by zero entries of w and contains 'resMod' (the restriction module). If eng<>0 use std, otherwise slimgb. Optional m: minimal integer root of b-function of I wrt (-w,w) can be specified. Optional G: specify Gröbner basis of I wrt (-w,w) (initial form of G generates initial ideal); assumptions on m and G not checked. Display controlled by printlevel.

rubrics_metrics.name: integralIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: integralIdeal(I,w[,eng,m,G]); I ideal, w intvec, eng and m optional ints, G optional ideal. Return: ring (a Weyl algebra) containing an ideal 'intIdeal'. Purpose: computes the integral ideal of a holonomic ideal w.r.t. the subspace defined by non-zero entries of w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is n-th Weyl algebra char 0, usual variable ordering. I assumed holonomic and w non-negative. Output ring is Weyl algebra for zero entries of w and contains 'intIdeal' (the integral ideal). If no zero entries, input ring is returned. If eng<>0 use std, otherwise slimgb. Optional m: minimal integer root of b-function of I wrt (-w,w) can be specified. Optional G: specify Gröbner basis of I wrt (-w,w). Assumptions on m and G not checked. Display controlled by printlevel.

rubrics_metrics.name: integralModule
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: integralModule(I,w[,eng,m,G]); I ideal, w intvec, eng and m optional ints, G optional ideal. Return: ring (a Weyl algebra) containing a module 'intMod'. Purpose: computes the integral module of a holonomic ideal w.r.t. the subspace defined by non-zero entries of w.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume basering is n-th Weyl algebra char 0, usual variable ordering. I holonomic and w non-negative. Output ring contains 'intMod' (the integral module). If no zero entries, input ring returned. If eng<>0 use std, otherwise slimgb. Let F(I) denote Fourier transform of I wrt w: minimal integer root of b-function of F(I) wrt (-w,w) can be specified via m. Optional G: Gröbner basis of F(I) wrt (-w,w). Assumptions on m and G not checked. Display per printlevel.

rubrics_metrics.name: deRhamCohom
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: deRhamCohom(f[,w,eng,m]); f poly, w optional intvec, eng and m optional ints. Return: ring (a Weyl Algebra) containing a list 'DR' of ideal and int. Purpose: computes a basis of the n-th de Rham cohomology group of the complement of the hypersurface defined by f (n = number of variables of basering).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basering is commutative over a field of characteristic 0. Output ring is the n-th Weyl algebra and contains list 'DR' with two entries (ideal J and int m) such that {f^m*J[i] : i=1..size(J)} is a basis of the n-th de Rham cohomology of complement of hypersurface f. If w is an intvec with exactly n strictly positive entries it is used; otherwise w defaults to (1,...,1). If eng<>0 use std, otherwise slimgb. If m is given it is assumed <= minimal integer root of Bernstein–Sato polynomial of f (not checked); otherwise m is set to that minimal integer root. Theory reference: SST pp.232-235. Display via printlevel. Example demonstrates output and K-dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: deRhamCohomIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: deRhamCohomIdeal(I[,w,eng,k,G]); I ideal, w optional intvec, eng and k optional ints, G optional ideal. Return: ideal. Purpose: computes a basis of the n-th de Rham cohomology group of the complement of the hypersurface defined by f for modules of the special kind (modules isomorphic to K[x,1/f] f^m with m <= minimal integer root of b_f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basering is the n-th Weyl algebra D over a field of char 0 with usual variable ordering. Further assume I is of the special kind (D/I presentation of K[x,1/f] f^m with m small enough); if I does not satisfy assumptions result may have no meaning. I can be computed with annfs. If w is intvec with exactly n strictly positive entries it is used, else defaults to (1,...,1). If eng<>0 use std, otherwise slimgb. Optional k: integer <= minimal integer root of b-function of F(I) wrt (-w,w). Optional G: Gröbner basis of F(I) wrt (-w,w). Assumptions on I,k,G not checked. Theory: SST pp.232-235. Display by printlevel. Example shows use with annRat and annfs and resulting basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: charVariety
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: charVariety(I[,eng]); I an ideal, eng optional int. Return: ring (commutative) containing an ideal 'charVar'. Purpose: computes an ideal whose zero set is the characteristic variety of I in the sense of D-module theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basering is n-th Weyl algebra over a field of characteristic 0 with usual variable identities. Output ring is commutative and contains 'charVar'. If eng<>0 use std, otherwise slimgb. Example shows computing charVar and using dim(std(charVar)) to conclude holonomicity. Display per printlevel.

rubrics_metrics.name: charInfo
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: charInfo(I); I an ideal. Return: ring (commutative) containing ideals 'charVar','singLoc' and list 'primDec'. Purpose: computes characteristic variety of I, its singular locus, and primary decomposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basering is n-th Weyl algebra over a field of characteristic 0 with usual variable ordering. In the output ring: 'charVar' is char(I), 'SingLoc' (singLoc) is singular locus of char(I), 'primDec' is primary decomposition list. Display per printlevel. Examples show charVar, singLoc entries and primDec components; primary decomposition format and sample entries displayed. Demonstrates how to interpret outputs to infer holonomicity, singular loci, and components.

rubrics_metrics.name: isFsat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isFsat(I,F); I an ideal, F a poly. Return: int, 1 if I is F-saturated and 0 otherwise. Purpose: checks whether the ideal I is F-saturated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check is implemented by verifying Ker(D -> F -> D/I) is 0, where D is basering. Example shows isFsat(LD,F) returning 1 and for J = LD*F returns 0. Basering and context as usual.

rubrics_metrics.name: appelF1
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: appelF1(). Return: ring (a parametric Weyl algebra) containing an ideal 'IAppel1'. Purpose: defines the ideal in a parametric Weyl algebra which annihilates Appell F1 hypergeometric function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output is a parametric Weyl algebra containing 'IAppel1' annihilating Appell F1. See SST p.48 for theory. Example shows explicit generators of IAppel1 with parameters a,b,c, etc. No extra optional args; output ring contains the ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: appelF2
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: appelF2(). Return: ring (a parametric Weyl algebra) containing an ideal 'IAppel2'. Purpose: defines the ideal in a parametric Weyl algebra which annihilates Appell F2 hypergeometric function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output is parametric Weyl algebra with 'IAppel2' annihilating Appell F2. See SST p.85. Example shows explicit IAppel2 generators with parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: appelF4
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: appelF4(). Return: ring (a parametric Weyl algebra) containing an ideal 'IAppel4'. Purpose: defines the ideal in a parametric Weyl algebra which annihilates Appell F4 hypergeometric function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output is parametric Weyl algebra with 'IAppel4' annihilating Appell F4. See SST p.39. Example shows explicit generators and parameters a,b,c,d.

rubrics_metrics.name: fourier
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: fourier(I[,v]); I an ideal, v an optional intvec. Return: ideal. Purpose: computes the Fourier transform of an ideal in a Weyl algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basering is n-th Weyl algebra char 0 with variable ordering. Fourier automorphism maps x(i) to -D(i) and D(i) to x(i). If v is an intvec with entries 1..n, Fourier transform of I restricted to variables given by v is computed. Example shows fourier(I,v) and fourier(I) outputs. See also inverseFourier. Display per printlevel.

rubrics_metrics.name: inverseFourier
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: inverseFourier(I[,v]); I an ideal, v an optional intvec. Return: ideal. Purpose: computes the inverse Fourier transform of an ideal in a Weyl algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fourier automorphism as above (x(i)->-D(i), D(i)->x(i)). If v provided restrict to variables v. Example demonstrates inverseFourier applied to fourier(I) returns original ideal. See also fourier. Display per printlevel.

rubrics_metrics.name: bFactor
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: bFactor(f); f poly. Return: list of ideal and intvec and possibly a string. Purpose: tries to compute the roots of a univariate polynomial f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output list consists of two or three entries: L[1] (ideal) contains roots of f, L[2] (intvec) multiplicities, optional L[3] (string) product of irreducible factors of degree >1. If f is zero or has no roots in ground field encoded as root 0 with multiplicity 0. Display per printlevel. Examples show factorization of (x^2-1)^2, (x^2+1)^2, and mixed polynomials; special encodings for constant polynomials and zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: intRoots
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: intRoots(L); L a list in bFactor format. Return: list of integer roots extracted from bFactor output. Purpose: extracts integer roots from a list given in bFactor format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input must be in bFactor format. Parameters treated as integers. Example: given bFactor((x-4/3)*(x+3)^2*(x-5)^4) returns integer roots [5,-3]. See also bFactor. Note: header shows a possible naming mismatch in the manual (usage line contains isInt(L) but example uses intRoots); intended proc is intRoots.

rubrics_metrics.name: poly2list
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: poly2list(f); f a poly. Return: list of exponents and corresponding terms of f. Purpose: converts a polynomial to a list of pairs consisting of intvecs (exponents) and polys (terms with coefficient).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Converts a poly to list where i-th pair contains exponent of i-th term and the i-th term (with coefficient). Examples show behaviour for monomials and multivariate polynomials and handling of zero (returns empty exponent list and term 0).

rubrics_metrics.name: fl2poly
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: fl2poly(L,s); L a list, s a string. Return: poly. Purpose: reconstruct a monic polynomial in one variable from its factorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: s is string naming a variable; L expected to consist of two entries: L[1] ideal with roots, L[2] intvec multiplicities. Example reconstructs s^7+... given roots and multiplicities; then factorize can recover linear factors. Useful to rebuild polynomial from bFactor-style output (e.g., Bernstein–Sato factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: insertGenerator
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: insertGenerator(id,p[,k]); id an ideal/module, p a poly/vector, k optional int. Return: same type as id. Purpose: inserts p into id at k-th position and returns the enlarged object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If k given, insert at position k; otherwise inserts at beginning (k=1). Works for ideals and modules (module generators given as vectors); examples show insertion at various positions and behaviour when module indexing creates zero entries. See deleteGenerator for inverse operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: deleteGenerator
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: deleteGenerator(id,k); id an ideal/module, k an int. Return: same type as id. Purpose: deletes the k-th generator from the first argument and returns the altered object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show deleting generators of ideals and modules; can produce zero or drop generators. See insertGenerator for inverse operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: engine
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: engine(I,i); I ideal/module/matrix, i an int. Return: same type as I. Purpose: compute the Gröbner basis of I with the algorithm chosen via i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default and if i=0 slimgb is used; otherwise std is used. Examples show identical outputs for slimgb and std on sample inputs; use i to choose algorithm for GB computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: isInt
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isInt(n); n a number. Return: int, 1 if n is an integer or 0 otherwise. Purpose: check whether given object of type number is actually an integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameters are treated as integers. Examples: isInt(4/3)=0, isInt(11)=1. Useful for argument validation in scripts and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: sortIntvec
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: sortIntvec(v); v an intvec. Return: list of two intvecs. Purpose: sorts an intvec while keeping zeros (unlike sort), returning sorted entries and a permutation such that v[perm]=sorted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In output list L: L[1] entries satisfy L[1][i] >= L[1][i+1]; L[2] is permutation so v[L[2]] = L[1]. Zeros are not dismissed. Examples demonstrate sorting of negative and zero entries and returned permutation. See also sort in Appendix for related behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: bfctVarIn
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: bfctVarIn(I[,a,b,c]); I an ideal, a,b,c optional ints. Return: list of ideal and intvec (and possibly string). Purpose: computes the roots of the Bernstein–Sato polynomial and their multiplicities for an affine algebraic variety defined by I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basering commutative over a field of characteristic 0. Varnames must not include t(1)..t(r) and Dt(1)..Dt(r) where r = number of generators of I. Output list L: L[1] ideal contains rational roots of b-function, L[2] intvec contains multiplicities, optional L[3] string is part of b-function without rational roots. Degree-0 b-function encoded via L[1][1]=0, L[2]=0 and L[3] indicates constant/nonzero. If a<>0 the ideal is used as given; otherwise a heuristically better generating set is used to reduce time. If b<>0 use std for GB, otherwise slimgb. If c<>0 use matrix ordering for GB, otherwise block ordering. Implementation notes: computes initial ideal of multivariate Malgrange ideal and then solves linear system by linear reductions following Noro. Result is shifted by 1 - codim(Var(F)) following (BMS06). Display controlled by printlevel. References: BMS06, ALM09. Example usage referenced.
